novelty.justification: The core proposal—"having an LLM first correctly retrieve a fact within a session makes that specific fact MORE vulnerable to being overwritten"—pursues a new LLM phenomenon and an associated measurement/mechanism, namely a "prediction-error-scaled destabilization signal" in the residual stream. Searches for "LLM retrieval-enhanced suggestibility," "language model memory reconsolidation," "prior answer retrieval misinformation overwrite," and "LLM context conflict activation patching" found the closest antecedents in human RES/reconsolidation research, especially "Surprise and destabilize: prediction error influences episodic memory reconsolidation" (2018), while LLM work such as DisentQA and "Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models" studies contextual conflict or answer accommodation without the paired prior-retrieval effect. The behavioral prediction is therefore a direct transfer of an established human-memory relationship rather than an entirely new conceptual relationship, but tying that contrast to a transient, prediction-error-gated, causally suppressible internal direction is a substantive multi-step mechanistic adaptation beyond merely changing the model or dataset.
